page0.text:
It's evening now.
Tohsaka seems busy and Sakura is asleep, so I'll make dinner.
My left arm can move, albeit slowly, so it shouldn't stop me from cooking simple meals.

page1.text:
"Hmm... I can deep fry the marlin, and make beef stew with the rest."
I check what we have in the refrigerator and decide on tonight's menu.
With two new mouths to feed, our ingredients go quickly.
I'll have to make some time tomorrow to go downtown for groceries.

page2.text:
"Thanks for the meal!"
Everyone seems excited to see that dinner's ready and waiting for them in the living room.

page3.text:
I wonder where Rider is, but she likely has her reasons for being absent.
Rider's priority is to protect Sakura. Maybe she doesn't want to have too much contact with Tohsaka, who could become an enemy.

page4.text:
"...I hope Rider comes down here to eat later."
If she doesn't come over, I'll pack a meal and bring it to her later.
She doesn't seem to like being around other people, so she's probably in the shed or the dojo.

page5.text: "Huh. So this is what you're good at making. Does Sakura specialize in Western food, while you do Japanese?"

page6.text:
Tohsaka looks at me with surprise as she munches on the fried fish.
I fried the marlin filets golden-brown and made an elegant soy sauce marinade that brings out the fragrance of ginger. Tohsaka seems fond of it.

page7.text:
"I like this one. I love that you're so good at cooking, Shirou."
Next to her, Illya is enjoying a mouth full of savory sweet beef stew.
...It's too bad that I didn't have any potatoes on hand, but I'm glad that she likes it.

page8.text:
But...
Sakura is holding her chopsticks, looking confused.

page9.text:
"Sakura? What's wrong, you don't have an appetite?"
"Ah... I do, but...um, Senpai?
Did you put sugar in this stew? It tastes strange."

page10.text:
"Huh!?"
D-did I really make such a rookie mistake with beef stew, of all things!?

page11.text:
"Crap. Hang on!"
I taste the beef stew from the pot in the middle of the table.

page12.text:
"...Mm?"
...That's odd.
This is how I always season it.

page13.text:
"Sakura, what's strange about it?"
"Did you maybe mix up the sugar and salt?
I can't taste the sweetness at all..."

page14.text:
"Really? Isn't it supposed to taste like this? Unless there's some secret ingredient that makes this one different from the rest.
I don't think I could make it as good as this."
"I don't know what it's supposed to taste like, but it's yummy. It's just sweet enough and easy to eat."

page15.text:
Sakura pokes at her beef stew with a puzzled expresion.
...She takes one bite. And a second. Then, a third.
"Sakura...?"

page16.text:
"Huh? O-oh, I think I just ate a part that wasn't seasoned as evenly. Sorry for being weird. Your cooking tastes good, Senpai."
She laughs and resumes eating.

page17.text:
"..."
Sakura moves her chopsticks as if nothing happened.
I got a little nervous when she started looking off, but then she regained her spirits.
With gusto. She even asked for a third helping.
Tohsaka watched in surprise as Sakura kept eating with delight, until we completely finished all of the food and rice.
